headline: Vierling's two-out single in 10th walks off Blue Jays
recap: The Phillies and Blue Jays traded zeros until the eighth, when Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s three-run homer off Seranthony Dominguez put Toronto ahead 3-0. Philadelphia answered immediately in the bottom half: J.T. Realmuto led off with a solo homer, and RBI singles from Dalton Guthrie and Kyle Schwarber tied it at 3-3. Neither side scored in the ninth. In the top of the 10th, Jean Segura speared a line drive and stepped on second for an unassisted double play to strand Toronto's runner, and in the bottom half Matt Vierling's two-out single with the bases loaded scored the automatic extra-innings runner for a 4-3 Phillies win.

Zack Wheeler opened for the Phillies and allowed just two hits over four scoreless innings with three strikeouts and no walks. Blue Jays starter Kevin Gausman matched him for longer, working six scoreless innings with eight strikeouts and two walks before the bullpens took over.

Andrew Bellatti worked a scoreless 10th for the win despite two walks, helped by Segura's double play. Adam Cimber took the loss after hitting Segura, walking Guthrie and then allowing Vierling's game-ending single.
